### Module 01 — R Foundations for Health Data

# R Foundations for Health Data

***
**Learning objectives**
- Set up a reproducible R environment for health analytics
- Understand core R data types used in health data workflows
- Read and inspect CSV, Excel, and JSON health data files
- Identify key health data sources: CMS, CDC, EHR exports
- Understand HIPAA-aware data handling basics

**Estimated time:** 1.5 hours  
**Level:** Beginner  
**Libraries:** `dplyr` / tibble, `readr`, `readxl`, `jsonlite`

## 1. Environment Setup & Library Imports

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Install any missing packages (run once)
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "readxl", "writexl", "jsonlite"))

library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(jsonlite)

cat("Library versions:\n")
cat(sprintf("  dplyr   : %s\n", as.character(packageVersion("dplyr"))))
cat(sprintf("  readr   : %s\n", as.character(packageVersion("readr"))))
cat("Environment ready.\n")
```

## 2. Core R Data Types in a Health Context

Health data pipelines use four foundational R structures. Understanding them prevents the most common data-wrangling errors.

```{r}
# --- 2.1  Vectors: ordered sequences (e.g. a patient's diagnosis codes) ---
diagnoses <- c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "Z87.891")
cat("Diagnoses vector:", paste(diagnoses, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("First code :", diagnoses[1], "\n")
cat("Last  code :", diagnoses[length(diagnoses)], "\n")
cat("Slice [2:3]:", paste(diagnoses[2:3], collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r}
# --- 2.2  Named lists: key-value pairs (e.g. a single patient record) ---
patient <- list(
  patient_id = "PT-00142",
  age        = 67,
  sex        = "F",
  diagnoses  = diagnoses,
  los_days   = 4,
  payer      = "Medicare"
)

cat("Patient record:\n")
for (key in names(patient)) {
  val <- patient[[key]]
  val_str <- if (is.atomic(val) && length(val) > 1) paste(val, collapse = ", ") else as.character(val)
  cat(sprintf("  %-15s: %s\n", key, val_str))
}
```

```{r}
# --- 2.3  Nested named lists: immutable pairs (e.g. ICD code + description) ---
icd_lookup <- list(
  `E11.9` = list(desc = "Type 2 diabetes mellitus", note = "without complications"),
  `I10`   = list(desc = "Essential hypertension",   note = ""),
  `N18.3` = list(desc = "Chronic kidney disease, stage 3", note = "")
)

for (code in names(icd_lookup)) {
  rec    <- icd_lookup[[code]]
  suffix <- if (nzchar(rec$note)) paste0("  [", rec$note, "]") else ""
  cat(sprintf("  %s → %s%s\n", code, rec$desc, suffix))
}
```

```{r}
# --- 2.4  Sets: unique memberships (e.g. unique conditions in a cohort) ---
cohort_conditions_a <- c("diabetes", "hypertension", "CKD", "obesity")
cohort_conditions_b <- c("hypertension", "heart failure", "obesity", "COPD")

cat("Shared conditions      :", paste(intersect(cohort_conditions_a, cohort_conditions_b), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Only in cohort A       :", paste(setdiff(cohort_conditions_a, cohort_conditions_b), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("All conditions (union) :", paste(union(cohort_conditions_a, cohort_conditions_b), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 3. Synthetic Health Dataset

We generate a realistic synthetic hospital discharge dataset so every learner starts from the same data without any data-use-agreement requirements.  
In real projects this would be replaced by a CMS, HCUP NIS, or EHR export.

```{r}
set.seed(42)
N <- 500

# --- Controlled random draws to mimic real discharge distributions ---
ages  <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, mean = 62, sd = 16), 18), 95))
sexes <- sample(c("M", "F"), size = N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
payers <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay", "Other"),
  size = N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.40, 0.22, 0.28, 0.07, 0.03)
)
drg_codes <- sample(c(470, 291, 392, 690, 871, 193, 247, 603), size = N, replace = TRUE)
drg_labels_map <- c(
  `470` = "Major joint replacement", `291` = "Heart failure & shock",
  `392` = "Esophagitis/misc GI",     `690` = "Kidney/UTI",
  `871` = "Septicemia",              `193` = "Simple pneumonia",
  `247` = "Perc cardiovasc w stent", `603` = "Cellulitis"
)
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))
charges  <- round(los_days * runif(N, 1800, 4200), 2)
missing_mask <- runif(N) < 0.08   # 8% missing charges (realistic)
charges[missing_mask] <- NA_real_

primary_dx <- sample(
  c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "I50.9", "J18.9", "A41.9", "M16.11", "N39.0"),
  size = N, replace = TRUE
)
admit_type <- sample(
  c("Emergency", "Elective", "Urgent", "Newborn"),
  size = N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.30, 0.16, 0.02)
)

df <- tibble(
  patient_id   = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age          = ages,
  sex          = sexes,
  payer        = payers,
  drg_code     = drg_codes,
  drg_label    = unname(drg_labels_map[as.character(drg_codes)]),
  primary_dx   = primary_dx,
  admit_type   = admit_type,
  los_days     = los_days,
  total_charge = charges
)

cat(sprintf("Dataset shape: %d rows × %d columns\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))
head(df, 8)
```

## 4. Reading Health Data Files

```{r}
# --- 4.1  Save and re-read as CSV (most common EHR export format) ---
health_dir <- file.path("Data")
dir.create(health_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
readr::write_csv(df, file.path(health_dir, "discharges.csv"))

df_csv <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(health_dir, "discharges.csv"),
  col_types = readr::cols(
    patient_id = readr::col_character(),
    drg_code   = readr::col_integer()
  ),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
cat("CSV load — shape:", nrow(df_csv), "×", ncol(df_csv), "\n")
print(sapply(df_csv, class))
```

```{r}
# --- 4.2  Excel (common for hospital billing exports) ---
writexl::write_xlsx(list(Discharges = df), file.path(health_dir, "discharges.xlsx"))

df_xl <- readxl::read_excel(
  file.path(health_dir, "discharges.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Discharges",
  col_types = c("text", "numeric", "text", "text", "numeric",
                "text", "text", "text", "numeric", "numeric")
)
df_xl$patient_id <- as.character(df_xl$patient_id)
cat("Excel load — shape:", nrow(df_xl), "×", ncol(df_xl), "\n")
head(df_xl, 3)
```

```{r}
# --- 4.3  JSON (common for FHIR / API responses) ---
sample_fhir_like <- df %>%
  head(5) %>%
  transmute(
    resourceType = "Patient",
    id           = patient_id,
    gender       = tolower(sex),
    age          = as.integer(age),
    condition    = primary_dx
  )

jsonlite::write_json(
  sample_fhir_like,
  file.path(health_dir, "patients.json"),
  pretty = TRUE, auto_unbox = TRUE
)

loaded  <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(health_dir, "patients.json"))
df_json <- as_tibble(loaded)
cat("JSON load — shape:", nrow(df_json), "×", ncol(df_json), "\n")
df_json
```

## 5. First-Pass Data Inspection

Always run these five commands before any analysis. They reveal dtype mismatches, hidden nulls, and cardinality surprises that will corrupt downstream results if ignored.

```{r}
# --- 5.1  Shape, dtypes, memory ---
cat("Shape:", nrow(df), "×", ncol(df), "\n\n")
glimpse(df)
cat("\nMemory:\n")
print(object.size(df), units = "Kb")
```

```{r}
# --- 5.2  Head and tail ---
cat("=== First 5 rows ===\n")
print(head(df, 5))
cat("\n=== Last 5 rows ===\n")
print(tail(df, 5))
```

```{r}
# --- 5.3  Missing value audit ---
missing_df <- df %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(pct = round(count / nrow(df) * 100, 2)) %>%
  filter(count > 0)
cat("Columns with missing data:\n")
print(missing_df)
```

```{r}
# --- 5.4  Cardinality check (critical for categorical codes) ---
cat_cols <- c("sex", "payer", "admit_type", "primary_dx", "drg_code")
for (col in cat_cols) {
  n_unique <- n_distinct(df[[col]])
  top_vals <- df %>%
    count(.data[[col]], sort = TRUE) %>%
    head(3)
  top_str <- paste(sprintf("%s=%d", top_vals[[1]], top_vals$n), collapse = ", ")
  cat(sprintf("  %-15s: %3d unique | top-3: %s\n", col, n_unique, top_str))
}
```

```{r}
# --- 5.5  Numeric summary with health-relevant percentiles ---
df %>%
  select(age, los_days, total_charge) %>%
  summarise(across(
    everything(),
    list(
      n    = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
      mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd   = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      p10  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.10, na.rm = TRUE),
      p25  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      p50  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.50, na.rm = TRUE),
      p75  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      p90  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
      p99  = ~ quantile(.x, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "stat", values_to = "value") %>%
  print(n = 30)
```

## 6. Health Data Sources Overview

| Source | What it contains | Access | Typical format |
|--------|-----------------|--------|----------------|
| **CMS Medicare claims** | Inpatient, outpatient, Part D claims for Medicare beneficiaries | Limited dataset (DUA required) | CSV / SAS |
| **HCUP NIS** | National inpatient sample, ~7M stays/year, all payers | AHRQ purchase or academic agreement | SAS / CSV |
| **CDC BRFSS** | Behavioural risk factors, chronic conditions, state-level | Public download | XPT / CSV |
| **PhysioNet MIMIC-IV** | De-identified ICU data: labs, vitals, meds, notes | Free after credentialing (~30 min) | CSV / Parquet |
| **Synthea** | Fully synthetic FHIR patients, no DUA needed | Open source, run locally | FHIR JSON / CSV |
| **NYC SPARCS** | NY State inpatient discharges with ZIP codes | Public download | CSV |

> **HIPAA reminder:** Real patient data requires a data use agreement, IRB approval, and safe-harbour or expert-determination de-identification before analysis. Use Synthea or public demo datasets for learning.

## 7. ICD-10 & DRG Code Structures

```{r}
# ICD-10-CM structure: Category . Etiology/Anatomic site . Severity
parse_icd10 <- function(code) {
  code <- gsub("\\.", "", code)
  category <- substr(code, 1, 3)
  if (nchar(code) > 3) {
    subcategory <- substr(code, 4, 4)
    detail      <- if (nchar(code) > 4) substr(code, 5, nchar(code)) else ""
  } else {
    subcategory <- ""
    detail      <- ""
  }
  list(category = category, subcategory = subcategory, detail = detail)
}

for (icd in c("E11.9", "I10", "N18.3", "A41.9")) {
  parsed <- parse_icd10(icd)
  cat(sprintf("  %-8s → category=%s  subcategory=%s  detail=%s\n",
              icd, parsed$category, parsed$subcategory, parsed$detail))
}
```

```{r}
# DRG distribution in our dataset
drg_dist <- df %>%
  group_by(drg_code, drg_label) %>%
  summarise(
    n_cases     = n(),
    mean_los    = mean(los_days),
    mean_charge = mean(total_charge, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_cases)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(mean_los, mean_charge), ~ round(.x, 1)))
cat("DRG distribution:\n")
print(drg_dist)
```

## 8. Knowledge Check

Answer these questions using the dataset before moving to NB-02.

1. What percentage of patients are `Medicare` beneficiaries?
2. Which DRG has the highest mean length of stay?
3. How many patients have a missing `total_charge`?
4. What is the 90th-percentile LOS in days?
5. List all unique `admit_type` values and their frequencies.

```{r}
# --- Exercise space ---
# 1. Medicare share
medicare_pct <- mean(df$payer == "Medicare") * 100
cat(sprintf("1. Medicare share: %.1f%%\n", medicare_pct))

# 2. Highest mean LOS by DRG
cat("\n2. Highest mean LOS by DRG:\n")
df %>%
  group_by(drg_label) %>%
  summarise(mean_los = mean(los_days), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_los)) %>%
  head(3) %>%
  print()

# 3. Missing charges
cat(sprintf("\n3. Missing total_charge: %d\n", sum(is.na(df$total_charge))))

# 4. 90th percentile LOS
cat(sprintf("\n4. 90th-percentile LOS: %.0f days\n",
            quantile(df$los_days, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)))

# 5. Admit type frequencies
cat("\n5. Admit type frequencies:\n")
print(count(df, admit_type, sort = TRUE))
```
